_note: How the land is grown, read by both editions (web: packed into textures.js by build-textures.ps1; desktop: res://data/worldgen.json). Blocks are named by their keys. Careful: a world's ground that nobody has changed is grown again from its seed every time it loads, so changing anything here changes worlds already made, not just new ones (a change like that needs a new land version in the code).

_notes.ORE_VEINS: veins of ore in the ground, grown in this order (a row's place picks its veins' random numbers, so moving a row moves every vein in every world). per: veins for each 10,000 columns of land; size: blocks in a vein; top, deep: its shallowest and deepest, in blocks below the surface. A vein is a short random walk that turns the Stone it passes through into its ore. takesDirt: it turns Dirt into its ore too. allDepths: in worlds from land 2 on, it ignores top and deep (3 below the surface all the way down, as common at every depth, with more veins in a taller world) and turns each deeper layer's stone into that layer's ore (so the ore needs deep versions); older worlds keep top and deep
_notes.BADLANDS_BANDS: the badlands' stripes of Terracotta, from the bottom of the world up (they repeat)
_notes.TREE_MIX: Biomes worlds from land 3: the trees each biome grows at its usual tree spots (where land 1 grows its trees), with each one's share. Leftover share (and a biome not listed) grows the biome's own tree as before: oak in the woods, plains and meadows, fir in the taiga and snowy lands, palm in deserts, willow in swamps
_notes.TREE_PATCH: the same kind of tree grows in patches this many blocks square
_notes.TREE_EXTRA: trees with spots of their own, tried in this order before the usual spots (a row's place picks its random numbers): chance per column of its biome's ground; grove [size, above]: only where a slow noise that size is above that; spacing: only one spot in each square this many blocks across can grow it (chance is then per spot); edge: only within that many blocks of another biome; coast: only low down with sea within that many blocks (with both: either one)
_notes.WILD_CROPS: Biomes worlds from land 5 (and 6): crops growing wild, in patches, grown right after the flowers, in this order (a row's seed picks its random numbers). For each column x, z from 8 to the world's size - 8: the patch's middle needs its biome in biomes (or, with near: a biome not in near, with a column of a near biome within the square |dx| <= within, |dz| <= within on the column biome map, looked at only after the chance below passes), and Hash(x, z, seed) <= chance. Then tries = tries[0] + floor(Hash(x, z, seed + 1) x (tries[1] - tries[0] + 1)) plants, the k-th (from 0) at x + floor((Hash(x + k, z, seed + 2) - 0.5) x 2 x spread + 0.5), z + floor((Hash(x, z + k, seed + 3) - 0.5) x 2 x spread + 0.5), standing on the ground there (its height) if that's one of ground with air above (Corn: 2 air): the ripe stage (Corn: both ripe halves; Cantaloupe: the grown vine, and a Cantaloupe beside it on the first free side of +x, -x, +z, -z, starting at side floor(Hash(plant x, plant z, seed + 4) x 4): air there, and one of ground under it at the vine's height; none free: the vine alone). The column's height goes up to the plant's top (a melon's column: up to the melon, if it was lower). Columns go z, then x (as the flowers), each row all through before the next; a near middle looks only at columns inside the world. The world grows one byte per block, so each of these grows as a stand-in, ripe Grain (49) for a crop (both of Corn's halves) or a Dead Bush, Bricks (64) for a Cantaloupe, and the real block goes in when the world is packed if its stand-in is still there (they're added to the list in the order they grew: Corn's lower half, then its top; a vine, then its melon). The structures after them count ripe Grain as a plant, like a flower (finding the ground under it, and building over it); snow stops at it
_notes.DEAD_BUSHES: Biomes worlds from land 5 (and 6): Dead Bushes, one here and there, grown after the wild crops: a column x, z (8 to the size - 8) with its biome in biomes and Hash(x, z, seed) <= chance gets one on its ground (its height) if that's one of ground with air above; its height goes up one
_notes.TREE_SHAPES: how each new tree looks: its log and leaves, trunk [shortest, tallest] above the ground; crown: how far its leaves reach (or [across, up and down]); tiers and gap: a cedar's layers of leaves, from the bottom, and the space between them; sparse: the share of its leaves left out; branch, branches: how long and how many
